svg.title: Which clock source wins
svg.desc: Time sources in order of authority, highest first: a Unit GPS on PORT.A, which carries its own date; the QMX+ GPS second-tick, but only when the QMX GPS flag is set, in which case it outranks SNTP; SNTP whenever WiFi is up; the Tab5 RTC; the QMX time-of-day as an offline fallback only; and manual entry as a last resort. Separately, the Tab5 RTC is what seeds the clock at boot, before any better source is available — that is an order of events, not an order of authority.
svg.text: Which clock source wins — highest authority first
Unit GPS on PORT.A
a satellite clock, and it carries its own DATE
QMX+ GPS second-tick
phase-locked to the second boundary, ~±25 ms
re-locked every 5 minutes
only when the QMX GPS flag is set
then it OUTRANKS SNTP — drift-free and
independent of WiFi, so better than ours
SNTP over WiFi
authoritative whenever WiFi is up
Tab5 RTC
holds the clock until something better arrives
QMX time-of-day
offline fallback ONLY — see the note
Manual entry
last resort — no network, no GPS
lower authority
Why the QMX clock ranks so low
Without GPS discipline the QMX's own RTC drifts freely.
Trusting it above SNTP would break FT8 timing whenever
it had wandered — so it is used only when SNTP is stale.
⚠ The boot order is NOT the authority order
The Tab5 RTC is applied first of all, at boot, before SNTP
or the QMX can answer. That makes it the first source in
TIME, not the highest in authority — anything above it on
this ladder replaces it as soon as it arrives.
WSPR and FT8 both search only a narrow slice of time either
side of the slot boundary, so a clock that is out by a couple of
seconds hears nothing and is heard by nobody. That is why this
ladder exists rather than one source.
